title: The finite constant-module open unit induces the actual abelian derived restriction
statement: Let A be a finite commutative ring in the coefficient universe, X a scheme [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], f a global function, j:X[1/f]→X the principal-open inclusion [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations]. Suppose the actual unit of derivedUpperStarLowerStarAdjunction(ModuleCat A,j), evaluated at the constant regular module A_X[0] [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf], is invertible. For every object V→X of X_proet, set T=V[1/v*f], viewed over X, and let i:T→V be its canonical inclusion. Then the right-derived natural transformation of ordinary abelian section restriction E_V→E_T, evaluated at the constant underlying abelian sheaf A_X[0], is invertible in D(Ab) [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. No affine or weak-contractibility hypothesis is required on V.

proof.text: Resolve the constant regular module on the open by a nonnegative complex I of injective module sheaves. Exact inverse image is left adjoint to direct image, so j_*I is K-injective. The canonical derived composition comparison therefore computes evaluation of the actual unit at V by the ordinary restriction A_X(V)→I(T). Inverse image of a constant module is constant. The canonical pullback model V×_X X[1/f] identifies with the displayed principal open T, compatibly with its inclusion. Evaluation of the given invertible unit consequently makes this specified module-valued derived restriction invertible.

Forgetting A-scalars commutes with constant sheafification and gives the constant abelian sheaf with value A. Localizing to V and T preserves injective module sheaves. The existing finite-ring injective acyclicity theorem then makes their underlying abelian sheaves evaluation-acyclic. The bounded-below comparison between the forgotten module resolution and abelian derived evaluation is induced by the identity on ordinary sections; it commutes with restriction. Thus it identifies the specified abelian arrow, rather than only its endpoints, with the forgotten invertible module arrow of the first step. This proves the assertion. All constructions also apply to the empty or identity open.

theorem finiteConstantUnit_isIso_derivedRestriction
    (A : Type (u + 1)) [CommRing A] [Finite A]
    (X : Scheme.{u}) (f : Γ(X, ⊤))
    (hunit : IsIso ((derivedUpperStarLowerStarAdjunction
      (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A) (X.basicOpen f).ι).unit.app
        ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor _ 0).obj
          ((constantSheaf (Scheme.ProEt.topology X) (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A)).obj
            (ModuleCat.of A A)))))
    (V : X.ProEt) :
    IsIso ((Functor.rightDerivedFunctorNatTrans
      (F := sheafToPresheaf (Scheme.ProEt.topology X) AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1} ⋙
        (evaluation X.ProEtᵒᵖ AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1}).obj (op V))
      (G := sheafToPresheaf (Scheme.ProEt.topology X) AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1} ⋙
        (evaluation X.ProEtᵒᵖ AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1}).obj
          (op (Scheme.ProEt.mk
            ((V.left.basicOpen (V.hom.appTop.hom f)).ι ≫ V.hom))))
      ((sheafSections (Scheme.ProEt.topology X) AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1}).map
        (MorphismProperty.Over.homMk
          (V.left.basicOpen (V.hom.appTop.hom f)).ι rfl :
            Scheme.ProEt.mk ((V.left.basicOpen (V.hom.appTop.hom f)).ι ≫ V.hom) ⟶ V).op)).app
      ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor _ 0).obj
        ((constantSheaf (Scheme.ProEt.topology X) AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1}).obj
          (AddCommGrpCat.of A))))
